title: 7.21.2 Check: the Quest game
description: Five multiple-choice questions on the hp bar, after(), guarding, making enemies from KINDS in newGame, and why the sender rolls in a duel. Checked instantly.

questions.question: A fighter has maxHp 30 and hp 10. Its full bar is 120 pixels wide. How wide is the rect drawn by rect(x - 60, y + 70, 120 * this.hp / this.maxHp, 10)?
options: 10 pixels
40 pixels
120 pixels
30 pixels
questions.explanation: 10 / 30 is one part in three, and 120 / 3 is 40.

questions.question: Why does the lab write after(45, enemyTurn) and not after(45, enemyTurn())?
options: enemyTurn() would run the enemy's turn now, not 45 frames later
The brackets would make the enemy wait twice as long before it acts
after only works with functions that are written inside a class
Without the brackets the enemy would act on your turn as well
questions.explanation: With brackets, enemyTurn runs right now and after is handed its answer. Without them, after is handed the function itself, to run later.

questions.question: The hero is guarding. The goblin hits for 7, and on its next turn hits for 7 again. How much hp does the hero lose in all?
options: 3 hp, as the guard covers both hits
14 hp
10 hp
7 hp
questions.explanation: The hit taken while guarding is halved, floor(7 / 2) is 3, and that hit ends the guard. The next one does the full 7: 3 + 7 is 10.

questions.question: Why is enemies = KINDS.map(...) in newGame() instead of in setup()?
options: So that map runs once each frame and keeps the enemies moving
So R brings back fresh enemies with full hp
Because KINDS can only be read from inside a function called newGame
So that the hero levels up each time a new game is started
questions.explanation: newGame() runs again when you press R, so map makes new Fighters from KINDS, all at full hp. KINDS itself is never changed.

questions.question: In a duel, why does the player who chooses roll the 0 to 3 and send it with the action?
options: So the other computer does not have to wait as long for the move
So a player can pick their own roll and always hit for the most
So both computers use the same roll and the hp bars agree
Because online.send can only carry numbers that came from random()
questions.explanation: If each computer rolled when the move arrived, they could roll different numbers. One roll, sent with the action, gives both the same fight.
